systems_changed.change_summary: Every neutral camp is replaced by nine new Haunt creature types with new behaviors (Specimen, Gutter Ghouls, Barrel Mimics, Past Dues, Stage Hands, Crabbage Pots, Festival Spirit, Shrooms, Underhands).
driving_changes: Haunts: all neutral camps replaced by new creature types with new behaviors
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Fixed jungle routes are dead — players must re-learn which camps pay and which punish, so map knowledge and AoE/sustain kits bank faster than memorized templates. Camp-fight shape (grouping, chasing, damage) is now a per-creature read rather than one known camp.

systems_changed.change_summary: Two new district objectives: Bell Tower atop Chinatown (high soul concentration but rings a map-wide bell) and Sunken Plaza beneath the Plaza (strips stamina on descent and mutes outside sound).
driving_changes: Bell Tower: new objective atop the Chinatown district; highly concentrated soul hotspot, but collecting it rings a bell heard across the map
Sunken Plaza: new objective beneath the Plaza district main square; descending strips your stamina and mutes outside sound
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Both pull telegraphed group fights to fixed hubs earlier, matching the existing Sunken Plaza/Bell Tower fight-gravity. Bell Tower taxes greed by broadcasting the farm; Sunken Plaza rewards a commit but the stamina-strip and muted audio make the exit a real risk.

systems_changed.change_summary: Kills now drop a contested Soul Bag you must secure before an ally takes it; last-hit rules apply to the bounty itself.
driving_changes: Soul Bags: kills now drop a Soul Bag you must secure before an ally takes it — contested-last-hit rules now apply to the bounty itself
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Kill income is no longer banked on the kill alone — the killer (or a faster teammate) must secure the bag, so fights extend and bounty income becomes slightly less reliable. Marginal nerf to clean 'secure the kill, bank guaranteed' burst patterns.

systems_changed.change_summary: Buff Containers now also roll Spirit Resist, Bullet Resist, Ability Range and Move Speed as permanent bonuses, not just the old range/resist pair.
driving_changes: Buff Containers: revamped golden statues now also roll Spirit Resist, Bullet Resist, Ability Range, and Move Speed as permanent bonuses
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Detouring for containers now pays off across more of a build, so off-lane routing and map-control roams gain value for every archetype; move speed and resists are worth contesting, raising the number of small skirmishes around pickups.

systems_changed.change_summary: Tough Crates stay Heavy-Melee-gated and yield extra souls, confirming melee itemization as a farm prerequisite.
driving_changes: Tough Crates: breakables that require a Heavy Melee to open; yield extra souls
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Reinforces the heavy-melee frontline as the crate-economy king; gun-only and non-melee kits must buy into melee or concede that income, keeping the box-farm lead engine intact after the camp rework.

systems_changed.change_summary: Steam Vents grant invisibility plus regen while stood on, four off-lane districts add farm/fight routes, Healing Snacks are hidden heal pickups, and Sunken Plaza strips stamina on descent.
driving_changes: Steam Vents: new terrain pickups granting invisibility and a small amount of regen while standing on them
Districts: four off-lane areas added — Theater, Chinatown, Haunted Lot, Plaza
Healing Snacks: new hidden pickups around the map that heal on grab
Sunken Plaza: descending strips your stamina
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Movement now carries a stealth/escape layer and stat detours, so repositioning and vision play matter more than raw lane presence; invisibility vents reward mobile assassins and vision counters, and healing snacks reward sustain-light kits.

systems_changed.change_summary: Successfully parrying objectives no longer resets Parry cooldown.
driving_changes: Parry: successfully parrying objectives no longer resets your Parry cooldown
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Kills the free parry chain at objective fights, so objective diving is harder to sustain and the T3-bullet-resist bodies that leaned on chained parries (Apollo, Mo & Krill) lose a small edge.

systems_changed.change_summary: Abilities and items now fire the instant the button is pressed instead of waiting for the next input window, lowering reaction latency globally.
driving_changes: Ability/Item use: now fires the instant the button is pressed instead of waiting for the next input window
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Combo and defensive-item timing tightens for every hero; burst and initiation windows land more cleanly and reactive saves (parry, defensive items) are more reliable, mildly favouring fast-cast kits over slow telegraphs.

systems_changed.change_summary: Broker trades high-tier items for Corrupted versions with shared per-match random negatives, first shipment ~30 min then roughly every 15 min; Street Brawl now grants a Corrupted item after the Round 5 draft.
driving_changes: Corrupted items: high-tier items can be exchanged for Corrupted versions with random negative attributes assigned per match; the positive/negative roll is identical for all players in a given game
Street Brawl: now grants a Corrupted item after the item draft in Round 5
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Adds a mid-late risk/reward conversion layer that is identical for everyone, keeping the ~30-min mark as the key scaling/stall window and rewarding leads that convert before the shared negatives bite.

systems_changed.change_summary: Bonus now has variable timings instead of a fixed window.
driving_changes: Sinner's Sacrifice: bonus now has variable timings instead of a fixed window
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Removes memorized-timer contesting of the sacrifice, so players must react to it and the objective becomes higher-variance and less reliably pre-farmed.

systems_changed.change_summary: Walkers no longer keep firing fireballs after dying.
driving_changes: Walkers: no longer keep firing fireballs after dying
systems_changed.effect_on_play: Removes post-death chip damage, so lingering near a killed Walker to push the wave or take a fight is safer — a small quality-of-life buff to sieging and to holding a just-cleared lane.

tempo_shift.why: New early-mid soul hotspots (Bell Tower, Sunken Plaza) and contested Soul Bags push fights over income sooner while no comeback lever is added and the Broker's ~30-min window stays the only scaling stall. The shared Corrupted layer and Buff Container stat detours add map-wide risk/reward but do not add a comeback valve.

archetype_effects.why: Tough Crates keep heavy-melee income king and Buff Containers now roll Bullet/Spirit Resist as permanent bonuses; the objective-parry nerf is only a minor tax.
Steam Vents grant invisibility, districts add routes, and instant ability/item activation tightens pick and escape timing.
Instant ability/item use cleans up combo windows, and Buff Containers now roll Ability Range as a permanent bonus.
Lower activation latency makes engage windows land more reliably across the new telegraphed hubs.
Instant activation helps, but the crate economy stays melee-gated and Buff Containers roll defensive stats rather than gun stats.
Lane cadence is untouched and the income engine still lives off-lane in camps and district hubs.
No comeback lever was added and new early-mid hotspots concentrate tempo fights, while the Broker window is unchanged.
Healing Snacks and Steam Vent regen let sustain-light kits self-sustain, trimming reliance on dedicated healing.
Districts open more routes but contested Soul Bags make bounty income less reliable, roughly cancelling out.
Walkers no longer fire after dying, making it safer to hold a just-cleared lane and press the wave.

systems.intent_read: Valve is relaunching the City Never Sleeps map as the game's main content and re-spreading soul income across many contested, discoverable sources rather than one memorized route. The reworked Haunts, new district objectives, contested Soul Bags and permanent-stat Buff Containers push players into more telegraphed, fought-over economy moments, with the shared Corrupted-item layer standardizing late risk/reward across the lobby.

items.summary: A new non-buildable merchant tier converts a finished high-tier item into a stat-boosted version carrying match-wide random negatives, so it's a between-match variance lever rather than an edge to whoever reaches The Broker first (rolls are symmetric). Because it only activates at ~30 min and pays teams that bank and stall, it runs against this patch's earlier, more contested soul economy — the tier raises the ceiling for games that still go long, and largely idles in the tempo games the patch is pushing.
items.build_shift: It converts an existing completed slot rather than adding one, so a bad negative roll can brick a core item — expect late-game players to hold a spare high-tier slot or delay a purchase until after the first ~30-min shipment rather than buy greedily into an unknown roll.

notable_item_stories: Corrupted items are the only new late-game power layer in a patch that pulled income earlier (Bell Tower, Sunken Plaza, contested Soul Bags), so its real value is inversely tied to how fast lobbies now close.
Street Brawl's Round 5 Corrupted grant imports the tier into draft-mode mid-game, where symmetric rolls matter more than raw stats — watch whether it reshapes late Brawl picks.
No hero has Corrupted items as a core or situational build slot (it isn't a buildable item), so there is no direct core-item hero link to trace this patch.

synthesis.size_why: A full map and neutral overhaul (all camps replaced by nine Haunt creature types), two new district objectives, contested Soul Bags, a new Corrupted-item merchant tier, and six new heroes — the content moves where souls come from, not hero stats.
synthesis.headline: The map economy is rebuilt from memorized farm routes into contested, discoverable soul sources — tempo arrives earlier and no two jungles read the same.

meta_thesis.previous: The lead engine was templated PvE income — guaranteed Tough Crate routes plus Sunken Plaza/Bell Tower hub fights — so AoE/sustain camp clearers and heavy-melee box farmers banked faster than lane bullies, with no comeback valve.
meta_thesis.new: The off-lane economy still wins games, but the fixed routes are gone: souls now come from behavior-varied Haunt camps, contested Soul Bags, permanent-stat Buff Containers, and earlier district objectives, so map knowledge and fast-clear kits bank faster than template memorizers.
meta_thesis.why: Drivers: all neutral camps replaced by nine Haunt types with new behaviors, Bell Tower/Sunken Plaza objectives, contested Soul Bags, and Buff Containers now rolling Move Speed plus Bullet/Spirit Resist. It extends 'map economy wins' but changes how and how early income is earned.

winners.why: Storm Cloud/Static Charge is the best clear for grouped, chasing Haunts and his crate-route opener now farms even faster (B->A).
Punch AoE farms the new camps fastest and Flying Strike paths open separated Shrines/objectives the new layout creates.
Green-lane roof/tree gives permanent lane high ground and districts/Steam Vents extend an already top-pick diver's routes; stays S.
Front-line gun tank with Weighted Bola anti-air in a patch that forces earlier fights — both the flyer tax and the frontline rise point at her.
Handed the default front-line slot with Baba still cut and Billy slipping; T3 bullet resist still commits under a Guardian despite the parry change.

losers.why: A single-target hook cannot punish crate/camp routing — the farm economy pays AoE, not pick combos.
Flyer tax is unchanged (air drag, Silver's Bola) and rising Lash is his worst lane — stays buried.
Late gun scaler in a no-comeback economy that now closes even faster; no item in his core moved.
Split-push scaler punished by contested Soul Bags and rising M&K/Lash — beaten by the meta, not the notes.
Flying burst scaler in a tempo patch, now hunted by buffed Deadman Danny (61% against her) and grounded by Bola.

non_obvious_calls.claim: The parry change is framed as a general objective tweak but is really a targeted nerf to the T3-bullet-resist objective-dive chain that Apollo and Mo & Krill relied on.
non_obvious_calls.why: Removing the cooldown reset on objective parries deletes the free parry chain only those resist-heavy divers used to sustain a Guardian dive.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Contested Soul Bags quietly nerf burst assassins who banked income on 'secure the kill, bank guaranteed.'
non_obvious_calls.why: Kill income now requires winning a second last-hit race on the bag, so secure-burst patterns convert less reliably.

non_obvious_calls.claim: Buff Containers are no longer just caster range stops — rolling Move Speed and Bullet/Spirit Resist makes them tank-contested pickups.
non_obvious_calls.why: Permanent defensive and mobility stats change who detours and why, raising the count of small skirmishes around pickups.

non_obvious_calls.claim: The Corrupted tier's value is inversely tied to how fast this patch ends games.
non_obvious_calls.why: It only activates around ~30 min, but Bell Tower/Sunken Plaza and contested income push fights and closures earlier, so many lobbies never reach the payoff.

uncertainties: Six new heroes are vote-gated, so their real meta impact is a rollout question, not a balance question — the first days are a lottery of who gets to play them.
Haunt camp soul values and clear difficulty are unstated, so 'which camps pay' is a live discovery rather than a given.
It is unclear whether the tempo shift actually closes games before The Broker's ~30-min window or just relocates the stall to the new hubs.
The win/pick snapshot conflicts with the KB in places (e.g., Graves 56.5%/48.5%), so some directional reads rest on contested data.
what_to_watch: Haunt camp soul values — which creature types are farm-worthy and which punish, and which kits clear them fastest.
First-contest timing at Bell Tower (bell broadcast) and Sunken Plaza (stamina strip) — the tells that hubs have moved earlier.
Soul Bag pickup rate — do fights genuinely extend to secure bounty, or does the bag get snaked and shift nothing.
Buff Container contest rate, especially Move Speed and Bullet Resist rolls, as the signal that pickups now matter to tanks.
New hero pick/win rates as the vote schedule rolls them out — plus whether a hotfix touches camp or crate economy.

verdicts.one_liner: Gun bruiser still fits the tempo economy; Abrams and Lash remain the ceiling.
verdicts.indirect: Vitality items untouched and the lane-wins economy suits his tanky M1; Graves's gun now pops his traps, and gap-closers Abrams (38%) and Lash still lock him out of range.
build_adjustments: Keep Battle Vest as the first buy.
Hold the ~40% grenade charge pivot for late anti-tank.

verdicts.one_liner: Neutral tempo carry; Steam Vents help slightly, but Venator is still the better slot.
verdicts.indirect: Steam-Vent invisibility marginally helps Smoke Bomb picks, but the faster-closing economy puts her weak T4 gun finish (Ricochet/Capacitor) further out of reach, and Paige/Victor still beat her.
build_adjustments: Skip the Ricochet/Tesla late pivot unless the game goes long.

verdicts.one_liner: Pure-gun rebuild isn't moved either way; Paige still walls her.
verdicts.indirect: Gun-carry archetype neutral and no core item moved, but she's a late scaler in an economy that ends faster, and rising Paige still beats her (57%).
build_adjustments: Stay on the pure-gun fire-rate core.

verdicts.one_liner: C-tier late scaler in an economy that closes before he finishes building.
verdicts.indirect: The crate/camp, no-comeback economy ends games before his spike and Shadow Weave gains little from the new district/Steam-Vent layout; no core item moved.

verdicts.one_liner: Rising anti-tank gets fed by the new tank wave, if his low snapshot WR turns.
verdicts.indirect: The rising tank front (Abrams, Mo & Krill, Billy) is free food for current-HP Serrated Knives, and harder Haunt camps reward his regen stack; Yamato/Bebop burst still kills him early.
build_adjustments: Keep the regen core; knives gain value as frontlines rise.

verdicts.one_liner: Fastest Haunt clear plus new Flying Strike objective paths, top of A.
verdicts.indirect: Punch AoE is the patch's best clear of grouped, chasing Haunts, and Flying Strike now creates paths to the Shrines/objectives the new layout separates; Buff Container Ability Range adds value.
build_adjustments: Stay on the on-hit spirit proc backbone.
Use Flying Strike paths to reach separated Shrines and objectives.

verdicts.one_liner: Camps and districts suit her, but she still can't kill a tank.
verdicts.indirect: Grouped-Haunt AoE clear and new-district mobility suit her, but nothing fixes her real problem: single-target burst that can't kill the rising tank front (Billy, Mo & Krill, Victor).
build_adjustments: Farm camps with district mobility between dives.

verdicts.one_liner: Steam Vents and new districts sharpen her picks; divers still punish her.
verdicts.indirect: New districts, hiding spots and Steam-Vent invisibility upgrade her roamer setups and put her ahead of Bebop in the pick slot; mobile divers Yamato/Lash/Holliday still dive a stationary sniper.
build_adjustments: Use Steam-Vent invisibility for new pick angles.

verdicts.one_liner: Split-push scaler the contested economy buries; kit fine, meta hostile.
verdicts.indirect: Contested Soul Bags and the faster-closing tempo economy punish split-push scaling, and rising Mo & Krill silence and Lash dive beat him; his 46% WR confirms it.
build_adjustments: No build fix, the problem is the map economy, not his items.

verdicts.one_liner: Burn AoE farms the new Haunt camps, but the map still ends before his spike.
verdicts.indirect: Grouped, chasing Haunt camps reward his burn AoE, and Buff Containers now rolling Ability Range/Move Speed help the spirit line; the faster economy still ends before his late spike.
build_adjustments: Stay on Dashfernus; the farm tailwind favors spirit, not burn gun.

verdicts.one_liner: More districts and Steam Vents give the best pick assassin more lassos.
verdicts.indirect: New districts, hiding spots and Steam-Vent invisibility expand her roam, and Bell Tower hub fights reward Spirit Lasso picks; point-blank lockdown (Drifter, Bebop, M&K/Lash ults) still ends her.
build_adjustments: Keep Extra Charge/Rapid Recharge to double-dip bounce-pad and lasso casts.

verdicts.one_liner: Melee bruiser the new Steam Vents and Tough-Crate routes were built for.
verdicts.indirect: New districts, Steam Vents and heavy-melee Tough-Crate routes fit his stealth-reveal roam, and the rising tank/frontline archetype suits him; Dynamo/M&K/Apollo lane pressure still caps him.
build_adjustments: Take heavy-melee Tough Crate routes as a farm angle on your roam.

verdicts.one_liner: Lane-bully frontliner losing his slot to Mo & Krill in a sustain-and-farm economy.
verdicts.indirect: The crate/camp-uptime economy wants sustained presence, not his all-in, and his front-line slot has moved to rising Mo & Krill; anti-tank Shiv (his worst lane, 43%) is climbing.
build_adjustments: No item change; draft around Shiv rather than into it.
